questions.q: Why do companies still perform subledger-to-GL reconciliation even with a well-tested Subledger Accounting configuration?
options: Because reconciliation is purely a legal formality with no practical value
Because "the subledger and GL should always agree" is a claim worth proving, not assuming, especially after rule changes or unusual activity
Because Subledger Accounting cannot actually produce journal entries without it
Because reconciliation replaces the need for a Chart of Accounts
questions.explain: Reconciliation is a recurring control that verifies, rather than assumes, that the subledger and GL agree for a control account.

questions.q: What is the basic comparison at the core of subledger-to-GL reconciliation?
options: Comparing two different ledgers' currencies
Comparing the subledger application's own balance for a control account against the GL balance on the corresponding account, for the same ledger and period
Comparing two unrelated suppliers' payment histories
Comparing the number of users logged into the system
questions.explain: Reconciliation compares the subledger's own balance to the GL control account balance for the same ledger and period.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT listed in this lesson as a common cause of a reconciling difference?
options: A subledger journal entry that was created but never transferred to GL
A manual journal entry posted directly to the GL control account, bypassing the subledger
A timing difference between when a transaction was accounted and when it transferred
The ledger having too many currencies assigned to it
questions.explain: The lesson lists missed transfers, manual postings bypassing the subledger, and timing differences as common causes — not currency count.

questions.q: Why is a manual journal entry posted directly to a control account like AP Trade a particular concern for reconciliation?
options: It is never a concern; manual journals always match the subledger automatically
Because it bypasses the subledger's own record entirely, which reconciliation is specifically designed to catch
Because manual journals are always larger in dollar amount than subledger journals
Because manual journals can only be entered by Oracle Support
questions.explain: A manual journal posted directly to a control account creates a difference between GL and the subledger because the subledger never recorded it; reconciliation is designed to surface exactly this kind of gap.

questions.q: How do the Account Analysis Report and Open Account Balances Listing typically fit into a reconciliation workflow?
options: They are not used in reconciliation at all
When the headline subledger and GL balances disagree, they are used together to isolate exactly which item or items are causing the gap
They can only be run once a year
They replace the need to compare subledger and GL balances at all
questions.explain: Once a mismatch is found, the Account Analysis Report and Open Account Balances Listing help pinpoint the specific item(s) responsible for the difference.
